title: A Simple Molecular-Orbital Treatment of H₂ Places Both Electrons in a Bonding Orbital
lead: Molecular orbitals are built from basis functions, filled with electrons two at a time, and gathered into Slater determinants. Their symbols record the electrons each holds and how each orbital behaves under reflection and inversion.
notes: Adapted from Hanson, Harvey, Sweeney and Zielinski's Quantum States of Atoms and Molecules, with a note by Mark Tuckerman (New York University), under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; the book gives no credit for Figure 9.6.1.
exercise_notes: The book sets no exercise in this section. The one here, on the g and u labels of Li₂'s and N₂'s configurations, was written by AI with its solution, Bloom level and concept tags.

exercises.source_id: the lowest energy configuration of N
exercises.prompt: Li2 has six electrons, and its lowest energy configuration fills the three lowest orbitals of the N2 configuration, Equation 9.6.3. (a) How many of Li2's electrons are in gerade orbitals? (b) How many of N2's fourteen electrons are in gerade orbitals?

parts.hint: Write Li₂'s configuration in the symbols of Equation 9.6.3 and read the subscripts.

answer.solution:
(a) Li2 takes the first three orbitals of Equation 9.6.3, two electrons each: $1\sigma_g^2\,1\sigma_u^2\,2\sigma_g^2$. The g orbitals are $1\sigma_g$ and $2\sigma_g$, which hold 4 electrons; the other 2 are in the u orbital $1\sigma_u$.

(b) In $1\sigma_g^2\,1\sigma_u^2\,2\sigma_g^2\,2\sigma_u^2\,1\pi_u^4\,3\sigma_g^2$ the g orbitals are $1\sigma_g$, $2\sigma_g$ and $3\sigma_g$, with 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 electrons. The other 8 are in $1\sigma_u$, $2\sigma_u$ and the pair $1\pi_u$, which change sign under inversion through the middle of the bond.
